aboutDescription: This React and TypeScript take-home task models meeting-room booking for a Tbilisi office. It brings room details, availability, bookings, and a personal schedule together.
aboutTestingDescription: There are 17 automated tests across seven files. All run with Vitest, and two of them use React Testing Library to exercise the visible booking forms. The remaining tests cover validation, schemas, mock HTTP behavior, persistence, overlaps, permissions, and Georgian holiday dates.
aboutCreateTestsDescription: Checks that an untitled booking cannot be submitted and that the entered title, time, and notes reach the create request.
aboutUpdateTestsDescription: Opens the edit dialog, changes the visible title and notes fields, and checks the update sent by the form.
aboutValidationTestsDescription: Checks time rounding, invalid dates, and the shared working-hour validation used by booking forms.
aboutSchemaTestsDescription: Rejects organizer and server-owned fields in create and edit requests, while allowing the fields users are meant to change.
aboutOverlapTestsDescription: Creates and updates bookings through the mock API, rejects room conflicts without partial writes, and checks edit and cancellation ownership.
aboutRepositoryTestsDescription: Confirms that cancellation keeps the original record for history and adds the cancelled status and timestamp.
aboutHolidayTestsDescription: Checks fixed annual dates and the four holidays whose dates move with Orthodox Easter, including their year-to-year changes.

guideBookingDateDescription: Choose a date with the weekday controls or the month calendar. The calendar marks holidays and blocked days, includes a year view, and leaves your draft and filters in place when you switch rooms.
guideBookingTimeDescription:
For the selected room, search by meeting name or time, then click or drag free slots to choose a {{bookingSlotMinutes}}-minute range. Meetings can last up to {{maximumBookingHours}} hours.

Select an existing meeting for its details. Your upcoming bookings can also be moved or resized.
guideBookingFiltersDescription: Search rooms and filter by capacity, amenities, lighting, accessibility, and air conditioning. The room list is a sidebar on desktop and a drawer on smaller screens.
guideBookingRoomDescription: Use the room carousel to check capacity, location, equipment, lighting, accessibility, and air conditioning. Changing rooms leaves the selected date, filters, and booking draft in place.
guideBookingAnyRoomDescription: Choose a time and group size to see the number of suitable rooms. Creating the meeting assigns one room that is free for the whole interval.
guideBookingSearchDescription: Search the paged booking history, including past and cancelled records. Combine text, date, personal, capacity, amenity, room, and organizer filters, then open a result in its booking context.
guideBookingEditorDescription: Check the room and time, add a title, optional attendees, and notes, then create the meeting. Saving checks duration, capacity, blocked days, the booking window, and overlaps again.
guideScheduleWeeksDescription: Move to the previous, current, or next work week. You can also choose a week from the month or year calendar.
guideScheduleTimelineDescription:
The five-day desktop timeline includes meetings you organize and meetings you attend.

Mobile focuses on one day at a time. Overlaps are arranged into lanes, and conflicts include text labels as well as color.
guideScheduleEditingDescription:
Open your upcoming meeting to change its title, notes, date, time, room, or attendees.

On desktop, drag the meeting or resize either edge in {{bookingSlotMinutes}}-minute increments. Red blockers show room conflicts before saving.
guideDashboardCalendarDescription: The month calendar shows office activity, availability dots, holidays, weekends, and the selected day. Select the month title for the year view or filter the summary to your meetings.
guideDashboardRoomsDescription: The Rooms tab lists booked rooms with their meeting count and total booked time. Select a room to check its meetings and facilities, then open that room's schedule.
guideDashboardBookingsDescription: The Bookings tab places the day's meetings on a working-hours timeline. Select one to see its room, organizer, attendees, notes, and available actions.
guideDashboardFilterDescription: Toggle Only my bookings to show calendar activity for meetings you organize. The selected day and its room and booking views stay available.
documentationIntro: Use this handbook to find rooms, make and manage bookings, read your schedule, and check office activity.
documentationWorkflowIntro: Booking is organised around a room, Schedule around the current employee, and Dashboard around the office.
documentationStateDescription: The URL keeps rooms, dates, filters, and open panels shareable. Hooks load data, TanStack Query caches it, and MSW saves accepted changes in browser storage.
documentationRulesDescription: The interface shows working hours, blocked days, room capacity, and occupied time. The mock API checks each create, edit, and drag operation before saving it.
documentationTimelineDescription: The timeline is the workspace for the selected room and day. It shows working hours, the current time, unavailable periods, bookings, and conflicts across suitable rooms. Click or drag free 15-minute slots to choose a range. Search by title or time, then select a booking to view, edit, or cancel it when allowed.
documentationDialogsIntro: Dialogs keep the context of the page that opened them. Theme and language controls stay available, and changing either setting leaves the dialog open.
aboutProjectStructureDescription: A concise map of the source directories and configuration files. Expand a folder to inspect its role, or collapse the tree to focus on one area.
projectStructurePublicDescription: Static files served directly by Vite, including MSW's browser worker.
projectStructureSrcDescription: The application source, separated into UI, data access, features, domain types, and mocks.
projectStructureApiDescription: Resource functions that make every application request through the shared Axios client.
projectStructureComponentsDescription: Reusable app-shell components and project-owned shadcn/Base UI primitives.
projectStructureFeaturesDescription: Feature modules keep pages small by grouping domain-specific components, hooks, and utilities.
projectStructureHooksDescription: TanStack Query hooks manage server-state fetching, mutations, caching, and invalidation.
projectStructureMocksDescription: MSW's browser API: seed data, storage repositories, policy helpers, and HTTP handlers.
projectStructurePagesDescription: Route-level page components that compose feature modules and URL state.
projectStructureTypesDescription: Shared TypeScript contracts for API DTOs, filters, and resource identifiers.
projectStructureTestsDescription: Focused unit and integration tests for booking rules, mock requests, and UI behavior.
aboutDecisionsIntro: The brief left several details open. These choices define how the application behaves and keep the same rules in the interface and mock API.
aboutMultipleRoomsDescription: A room cannot have two confirmed meetings at once. An organizer may reserve multiple rooms for parallel sessions or breakout space. Attendee clashes are shown but do not block saving. The mock API performs the final overlap and ownership checks <path>(src/mocks/handlers/bookingHandlers.ts)</path>.
aboutUrlDecisionTitle: Navigation state is kept in the URL
aboutUrlDecisionDescription: Rooms, dates, filters, selected bookings, and panel state are stored in route or search parameters. Refreshing or sharing a link restores the same context. Schedule parsing lives outside visual components <path>(src/hooks/schedule/useScheduleUrl.ts)</path>.
aboutMockDecisionTitle: The mock API follows production-style boundaries
aboutMockDecisionDescription: The UI uses Axios and REST-shaped endpoints through one client <path>(src/api/api.ts)</path>. MSW starts at the application boundary <path>(src/mocks/browser.ts)</path> and writes accepted changes to <type>localStorage</type>. Connecting a real API service will only require changing the Axios base URL and disabling MSW.
aboutAvailabilityDecisionDescription: A room is available only when the whole meeting fits in one free interval. Weekends and Georgian public holidays block dates from being booked, but that can be changed by separate settings <path>(src/constants/index.ts)</path>. Fixed holidays repeat each year, and Orthodox Easter dates are calculated per year <path>(src/mocks/domain/georgianHolidays.ts)</path>. MSW checks the same rules before saving <path>(src/mocks/handlers/bookingHandlers.ts)</path>.
aboutBoundaryDecisionTitle: The app separates UI, API, rules, and persistence
aboutBoundaryDecisionDescription: Pages use query hooks <path>(src/hooks/)</path>, which call API resources <path>(src/api/)</path>. MSW handlers handle HTTP <path>(src/mocks/handlers/)</path>, domain helpers enforce booking rules <path>(src/mocks/domain/)</path>, and repositories access browser storage <path>(src/mocks/db/)</path>.
aboutTimezoneDecisionTitle: Calendar labels and instants use different representations
aboutTimezoneDecisionDescription: Bookings are stored as <type>ISO 8601</type> instants, then shown and grouped by date in the configured Tbilisi (UTC+4) timezone <path>(src/lib/date.ts)</path>. A device in another timezone will have meetings in the same time.
aboutAccessibilityDecisionTitle: Interaction semantics are part of the architecture
aboutAccessibilityDecisionDescription: Dialogs, drawers, tabs, calendars, sliders, and buttons are built with shadcn's accessible primitives <path>(src/components/ui/)</path>. Controls have clear labels, visible focus states, and keyboard support, while availability and conflicts are communicated with text as well as color.
aboutDataModelIntro: The data layer is arranged as if it were talking to a backend: pages use hooks and API contracts, while mock request handling and browser persistence stay behind that boundary.
aboutDomainModelsDescription: API records have explicit TypeScript models. Localized fields always contain English and may also contain Georgian. Holiday rules are converted into ordinary dated records before they reach the UI.
aboutBookingModelDescription: Links a room and organizer to an exact time range, with attendees, notes, status, and audit timestamps.
aboutRoomModelDescription: Contains the capacity, location, equipment, lighting, air conditioning, and accessibility details used to choose a room.
aboutEmployeeModelDescription: Provides the identity and department information used for organizers and attendees. (department isn't used anywhere in the UI, but is included in the data for realism).
aboutHolidayModelDescription: The API returns a dated Georgian holiday. Fixed holidays recur from a month-and-day rule, while Good Friday, Holy Saturday, Easter Sunday, and Easter Monday are calculated from Orthodox Easter because their dates are not consistent from year to year.
aboutApiStructureDescription: A shared Axios client <path>(src/api/api.ts)</path> serves resource modules for rooms, employees, holidays, bookings, activity summaries, and guide progress <path>(src/api/)</path>. TanStack Query hooks handle caching and pagination <path>(src/hooks/)</path>. MSW parses requests <path>(src/mocks/handlers/)</path>, domain helpers validate them <path>(src/mocks/domain/)</path>, and repositories persist accepted changes <path>(src/mocks/db/)</path>.
aboutSeedDataDescription: The bundled JSON data <path>(src/mocks/data/)</path> starts with exactly 754 bookings. Meeting-room names come from Nordic lakes, and Giorgi Vartanov is the current user (me) <path>(src/constants/index.ts)</path>. Localized fields use <type>ILocalizedText</type> <path>(src/types/room.ts)</path>. There is no authentication or actual backend because this assignment focused mainly on the frontend, but the REST-shaped MSW layer can be swapped for a real API without rebuilding the UI.
aboutPagesIntro: Each route has one job, from choosing a room to reviewing a personal week or understanding the office as a whole.
aboutBookingPageDescription: Search and filter rooms, compare them, inspect a daily timeline, and create or edit a booking without losing the selected date or filters.
aboutSchedulePageDescription: Shows meetings for the current employee (that is hardcoded as employee with id employee-482701) that they are organizing or attending. Theres a full week view with the ability to move and resize bookings.
aboutDashboardPageDescription: Summarizes room use on a large calendar. Selecting a day opens its rooms and meetings, with links back to the relevant schedule or booking.
aboutAboutPageDescription: Records the main implementation choices, data contracts, test coverage, technology choices, and the role AI played during development.
aboutDocumentationPageDescription: Has description of the application from the user's perspective, reading schedules, using dialogs, and navigating with the keyboard. it also has links to the guides.
aboutErrorPagesDescription: They are shown when a route does not exist or a page fails.
aboutTechnologyIntro: The stack aligns with the task requirements: React with TypeScript, reusable controls, URL-backed navigation, forms, and a mock API that can later be replaced.
aboutApiDescription: Components use API functions and TanStack Query. Axios sends every request; MSW provides REST-shaped development endpoints backed by versioned browser storage, so a real server can replace it without rewriting the UI.
aboutStateDescription: Shareable filters and selections live in URL parameters, server state is cached, and booking forms use React Hook Form with Zod. The mock API repeats business-rule validation before persisting a change.
aboutRequestsDescription: Feature hooks create consistent query keys <path>(src/hooks/)</path> and call resource functions <path>(src/api/)</path>. The resource functions send requests through the shared Axios client <path>(src/api/api.ts)</path>. MSW handlers receive and parse those requests <path>(src/mocks/handlers/)</path>, domain validators check the booking rules <path>(src/mocks/domain/)</path>, and repositories save accepted changes in versioned <type>localStorage</type> collections <path>(src/mocks/db/storage.ts)</path>.
aboutRulesDescription: Booking settings that may change, such as duration limits, working hours, and blocked days, are kept together in <path>(src/constants/index.ts)</path>. The UI shows these limits before saving, and MSW checks them again before storing a booking <path>(src/mocks/handlers/bookingHandlers.ts)</path>. Booking times are stored as <type>ISO 8601</type> timestamps, then converted with the Tbilisi date helpers for display and calendar dates <path>(src/lib/date.ts)</path>.
aboutRoutingDescription: React Router stores shareable room, date, filter, modal, and guide state in the URL <path>(src/pages/)</path>. Project-owned shadcn and Base UI primitives provide the interactive controls <path>(src/components/ui/)</path>. Desktop resizable layouts <path>(src/features/layout/components/ResizableScheduleLayout.tsx)</path> become focused views and drawers on smaller screens.
aboutGuidesImplementationDescription: One set of definitions supports tours for room booking, schedules, the dashboard, and key dialogs <path>(src/features/guide/data/guideContent.ts)</path>. The guide provider reads the current route and step from the URL, finds the matching <type>data-guide</type> target, positions the guide beside it, and saves the reader's last step <path>(src/features/guide/components/GuideProvider.tsx)</path>. This keeps a guide connected to the part of the app it explains. Handbook links can open a specific step directly, and readers can return to the same section after navigating away.
aboutOptimisticDescription: Editing user's own booking, does optimistic update, before the request completes and restores the previous data if it fails <path>(src/hooks/bookings/useEditBooking.ts)</path>. On success, related room, employee, search, activity, and detail queries are refreshed.
aboutLayoutPersistenceDescription: The desktop schedule and dashboard use resizable panels (shadcn's built-in component). Each layout stores its percentage in local storage <path>(src/features/layout/components/ResizableScheduleLayout.tsx)</path> <path>(src/features/layout/components/ResizableDashboardLayout.tsx)</path>. Stored values are limited to safe bounds before use.
aboutPerformanceDescription: Routes load on demand, and the header preloads page that is associated with the hovered navlink <path>(src/components/AppHeader.tsx)</path>. TanStack Query reuses cached data, booking search is debounced <path>(src/features/search/components/BookingSearchDialog.tsx)</path>, and calendar activity is aggregated before rendering <path>(src/mocks/handlers/calendarHandlers.ts)</path>. Room images use WebP.
aboutQualityDescription: Vitest and React Testing Library cover domain rules, HTTP handlers, repositories, holiday generation, and visible booking forms <path>(tests/)</path>. English and Georgian resources live together <path>(src/locales/)</path>. Domain contracts <path>(src/types/)</path>, policy constants <path>(src/constants/)</path>, API resources <path>(src/api/)</path>, hooks <path>(src/hooks/)</path>, and mock persistence <path>(src/mocks/db/)</path> remain separate.
aboutUseReact: Builds the component tree, providers, portals, error boundaries, and responsive feature composition.
aboutUseTypeScript: Defines strict domain DTOs, branded IDs, form inputs, filters, API errors, and component contracts.
aboutUseVite: Runs development, splits lazy route and guide chunks, processes assets, and creates the static production bundle.
aboutUseTailwind: Implements responsive layouts, design tokens, container queries, state styling, and dark mode.
aboutUseShadcn: Supplies the project-owned accessible UI primitives and consistent composition patterns.
aboutUseBaseUi: Provides the accessible behavior beneath modals, drawers, selects, sliders, tabs, and buttons.
aboutUseQuery: Caches server state, paginates searches, prefetches likely navigation, performs optimistic mutations, and invalidates affected data.
aboutUseRouter: Defines lazy routes and keeps shareable selection, filters, modals, return locations, and guide steps in URLs.
aboutUseMsw: Intercepts REST-shaped browser requests and delegates validation and persistence to mock domain and repository layers.
aboutUseAxios: Provides the only application HTTP client, common headers, resource requests, and normalized API errors.
aboutUseForm: Manages booking create/edit fields, dirty state, validation feedback, and controlled submission.
aboutUseZod: Validates forms and independently parses create/update request bodies inside MSW handlers.
aboutUseDateFns: Handles date arithmetic, week/month navigation, formatting, duration checks, and calendar comparisons.
aboutUseI18next: Loads complete English and Georgian resources and updates interface copy, dates, and localized domain text at runtime.
aboutUseEmbla: Powers the shadcn room carousel and its previous/next navigation behavior.
aboutUseDayPicker: Powers calendar grids, modifiers, disabled dates, month/year selection, and custom day buttons.
aboutUseLucide: Provides consistent accessible interface icons without hand-authored SVG components.
aboutUseVitest: Runs focused unit and mock integration tests for business rules and data behavior.
aboutCodexTitle: How I used AI while building this project
aboutCodexDescription: I built the application over three focused development days, although none of them was a full working day. I used Codex for implementation, refactoring, tests, and documentation. I made the product, visual, and architecture decisions, then directly handled restyling, performance fixes, responsive behavior, and features that were quicker or clearer to implement myself than to specify to AI, as well as work that needed correction after an AI attempt.
aboutCodexOwnership: I designed the main data flow from pages to query hooks, API resources, MSW handlers, validation, and repositories. I also decided which state belonged in the URL, how mutation invalidation should reach schedules and dashboards, and where booking policy should live. My review loop was to compare each result with the brief, use it in the browser, and inspect the code; Codex ran tests, linting, formatting, and production builds as part of that loop.
aboutCodexSolRole: Used for architecture work, changes that crossed several features, broad code reviews, and the harder correctness problems.
aboutCodexTerraRole: Used for most day-to-day implementation, extracting components, TypeScript cleanup, interface consistency, and documentation.
aboutCodexLunaRole: Used for quick code searches, repetitive checks, and small verification tasks where a fast answer was enough.
aboutCodexChallengesDescription: These generated implementations looked reasonable in isolation but missed product decisions, interaction details, or realistic performance constraints.
aboutCodexCalendarChallengeDescription: The first version recreated timezone formatters and rescanned the full booking list inside nested day and time-slot loops, making the calendar dialog noticeably slow with the complete seed dataset. I profiled it in the browser, reused the formatters, generated Tbilisi calendar keys consistently, and moved booking aggregation outside the nested render loops.
aboutCodexCalendarHeaderChallengeDescrip: The AI-generated version did not place the calendar controls in the modal header with the intended layout and behavior reliably, so I implemented that part directly.
aboutCodexAnyRoomChallengeDescription: Generated versions handled the basic pointer movement but missed edge cases around resizing from either side, preserving the meeting duration, snapping to 15-minute intervals, and previewing room conflicts before a drop.
aboutCodexResponsiveChallengeDescription: Simply shrinking the desktop week created cramped columns and horizontal scrolling on phones. I replaced it with a single-day mobile view and decided which controls should move into drawers.
aboutCodexUrlChallengeDescription: Generated implementations often reached for local component state. I identified which rooms, dates, filters, bookings, and dialog selections needed to survive refreshes and browser navigation through URL parameters.
aboutCodexRulesChallengeTitle: Rules across the UI and API
aboutCodexRulesChallengeDescription: Some generated changes fixed validation in the form but not in MSW, or the other way around. I centralized the policy values and checked that create, edit, drag, resize, and cancellation followed the same rules at both boundaries. I also added a separate Orthodox Easter calculation so movable Georgian holidays are blocked alongside fixed-date holidays.
aboutCodexDatesChallengeDescription: Default JavaScript dates made otherwise correct code depend on the device timezone, and fixed-date holiday logic could not cover Orthodox Easter. I enforced Tbilisi calendar keys and added separate calculation for the movable dates.
aboutCodexPolishChallengeDescription: Generated layouts often contained every required control but still had uneven spacing, weak hierarchy, unstable loading geometry, or awkward mobile behavior. I restyled and adjusted those details directly while testing the complete interface.
guideWelcomeTitle: Would you like a guided tour?
guideWelcomeDescription: The tour explains room booking, your weekly schedule, and the dashboard. You can leave at any time and restart it from the question-mark button.
documentationKeyboardIntro: Use these controls throughout the application. Shortcuts are ignored while typing in a form field.
documentationKeyboardEscape: Close the active year view, guide, drawer, or modal.
documentationKeyboardNavigation: Open Room booking, Schedule, Dashboard, Documentation, or About respectively.
documentationKeyboardGuide: Open the guide for the current page when you are not typing in a form field.
documentationKeyboardToday: Return to today or the current week on calendar pages.
documentationKeyboardFilters: Open room filters on the booking page.
documentationKeyboardMine: Toggle Only my bookings on the booking search or Dashboard.
documentationKeyboardPrevious: Move to the previous day, or previous week on Schedule.
documentationKeyboardNext: Move to the next day, or next week on Schedule.
documentationCalendarDialogDescription: Choose a date, use the personal activity filter when available, change months, or select the month heading to choose from the whole year.
documentationSearchDialogDescription: Search every booking and combine date, room, organizer, capacity, amenity, and personal filters. Selecting a result opens it on the booking page.
documentationDetailsDialogDescription: Review room and booking information, then edit, cancel, open the booking page, or return to the originating dashboard position when applicable.
documentationEditDialogDescription: Edit owned upcoming bookings, change rooms, manage attendees, and save only after date, duration, room, organizer, and overlap rules pass.
modalGuideRoomDescription: Review the room and its facilities for this meeting.
modalGuideDetailsDescription: Review the organizer, date, time, attendees, creation time, and notes.
modalGuideActionsDescription: Edit or cancel your booking, open it on the booking page, or return to the page that sent you here.
modalGuideCancelDescription: Confirm cancellation or keep the booking unchanged.
modalGuideSearchFiltersDescription: Combine text, date, personal, capacity, amenity, room, and organizer filters.
modalGuideSearchResultsDescription: Every matching booking is listed here, including past and cancelled bookings. Select one to open it on the booking page.
modalGuideCalendarDescription: Choose a date, move between months with the arrows, or select the month title to open the responsive year view. Weekends and Georgian holidays are identified and follow the configured booking rules.
modalGuideEditFormDescription: Change the title, notes, date, and attendees. Attendee selection is limited by the selected room's capacity.
modalGuideEditTimeDescription: Choose a valid start and end in 15-minute increments. Availability is checked again when saving.
modalGuideEditRoomDescription: Open the room picker to search and filter another room for this booking.
modalGuideRoomPickerDescription: Search and filter rooms, select one, then confirm your choice.
modalGuideUnsavedDescription: Keep editing, discard the draft, or save it before closing.
modalGuideOpenCalendarDescription: Use this button to open the calendar. Selecting it or pressing Next opens the modal and continues the guide.
modalGuideOpenSearchDescription: Use this button to open booking history. Selecting it or pressing Next opens the modal and continues the guide.
modalGuideOpenDetailsDescription: Select a booking to open its details. Selecting it or pressing Next reopens the modal and continues the guide.
modalGuideOpenEditDescription: Use the edit action on your upcoming booking. Selecting it or pressing Next opens the editor and continues the guide.
modalGuideOpenCancelDescription: Use the cancel action on your booking. Selecting it or pressing Next opens the confirmation and continues the guide.
modalGuideOpenRoomPickerDescription: Use Change room to open the room picker. Selecting it or pressing Next opens the drawer and continues the guide.
modalGuideOpenUnsavedDescription: Close the editor after making a change to open the unsaved-changes confirmation.
mswLoadingNote: Demo loading note: MSW acts as the backend in the browser and initializes large bundled JSON seed files, including a 9,804-line bookings file containing exactly 754 initial bookings. The first page load may therefore take longer than later cached navigation.
